facts: Project Jupiter in Doña Ana County will create 4,000 construction jobs and 1,500 ongoing project-supported jobs
Currently 38 states offer dedicated tax incentives for data centers
Activists and some policymakers are seeking local moratoriums on data center facilities
Doña Ana County commissioners voted 4-1 to approve $165 billion in industrial revenue bonds for Project Jupiter last September
Oracle says the data center and fuel cell system together will use about 11 million gallons of non-potable water, recycled in closed-loop systems
Developers pledged $360 million for schools and local infrastructure and $50 million for a local water utility upgrade
The Center for Biological Diversity filed a protest letter with the State Engineer over groundwater draws from the lower Rio Grande basin
Last month the US Supreme Court approved an interstate water compact that will retire 9,200 acres of irrigated farmland over the next decade
Project Jupiter was approved September 19, 2025 by the Doña Ana Board of County Commissioners in a 4-1 vote
Project Jupiter is planned at 700 to 900 megawatts and is located just north of the Santa Teresa port of entry, less than 10 miles from El Paso, Texas
Locals learned of the $165 billion project just one month before the county approved it
New Mexico's HB137 created the Strategic Water Supply program, allocating $40 million for desalination grants
Doña Ana County commissioners approved Project Jupiter bond proposal 4-1 on Sept. 19, 2025
Project Jupiter would avoid property taxes for 30 years in exchange for $360 million in payments to the county
On Sept. 16, 2025 the city of Sunland Park joined calls to delay the vote
Data Center Watch counted $64 billion of data center projects delayed or paused amid local opposition in two years
Developers plan to invest up to $165 billion in Project Jupiter, promising 2,500 construction jobs and over 750 permanent jobs
Doña Ana commissioners voted 4-1 in late August to advance an industrial revenue bond, with a final vote set for Sept. 19
The bond would exempt BorderPlex from property taxes for 30 years, with $300 million in payments to the county in lieu
Developers said average daily water use would be about 20,000 gallons, capped at 60,000
On Sept. 5, Commissioner Reynolds posted names of people who submitted opposing public comments on Facebook
Borderplex Digital Assets says it will invest $165 billion in a data center campus in Doña Ana County, NM.
Doña Ana County commissioners are scheduled to vote on the project on September 19.
Borderplex would pay Doña Ana County $300 million in direct payments over about 30 years in exchange for no property taxes.
The project is projected to create over 2,000 construction jobs and 750 permanent jobs paying $75,000-$100,000.
El Paso Electric says it has been designing electricity infrastructure to serve the data center for over two years.
Doña Ana County commissioners voted in September to finance the project through industrial revenue bonds
Air permit comment period is 30 days; community groups ask for an extra 30 days
Developers seek air quality construction permits for two microgrids to power the facility

facts: Santa Fe County Commission will hear a proposed one-year data center moratorium ordinance at 2:00PM on June 30.

Santa Fe County commissioners are weighing a yearlong prohibition on data center developments.
No data centers exist or have been proposed in Santa Fe County or Northern New Mexico.
86 localities have passed data center bans and 57 more are under consideration, per the U.S. Data Center Moratorium Tracker.
